topIssues.title: kona-node: verify delegated derivation parity against op-node
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

The tracker's completion criteria include verification work that no fix PR covers. This issue tracks it so the parity claim rests on exercised behavior, not only on unit tests in the three core fixes (#23675, #23676, #23677).

Scope:
- Verify safe and finalized progress by block hash and ancestry, comparing CL and EL labels, with unsafe production paused.
- Exercise source-ahead catch-up and an EL answering SYNCING followed by VALID, including unchanged-target retries and eventual recovery.
- Exercise stale-source finalized references and confirm finalized never moves backward and conflicting hashes are not accepted.
- Run the follow-source acceptance cases against Kona, or explicitly retain and link the remaining gaps: #22272, #22273, #22274.
- Record results on #545 and tick the corresponding completion checkboxes.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_InvalidBlock`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139419/workflows/feb351e1-7e49-410d-a1ee-27a572f0e50e/jobs/5877424

Job `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`, merge-queue run for ethereum-optimism/optimism#23771 (contracts-only change), 2026-11-10.

```
Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:392
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:1196
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/interop_fault_proofs_test.go:81
Error:       Received unexpected error:
             operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: not found
Messages:    invalid exec msg receipt not found
```

About 10s before the assertion, chain 902 reorged out the unsafe block (13) that carried the invalid exec message tx:

```
WARN L2 reorg: existing unsafe block does not match derived attributes from L1 component=supernode chain_id=902
  err="transaction 0 does not match ..." unsafe=ce53f5..f22801:13 pending_safe=ac50d9..a4c010:12
```

The mismatch is in the L1 info deposit (different L1 origin), so the tx is dropped and its receipt is never found. Looks like a race between sequencing and L1 derivation rather than a code regression. CircleCI insights also shows a failure in `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (1/100 runs on develop).

topIssues.title: rust: bump reth to 2.7.0
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Bump reth to v2.7.0, following #23046 and the fork in ethereum-optimism/reth#15.

The v2.7.0 tag does **not** contain the five upstream fixes below. Carry them on top of v2.7.0 when preparing the new fork pin. This inventory is based on #23046 at `93d9ec9d2f0fadf3b587c64b3f423e89ffaa5199`, which pins reth to `8d359d0142719d4042eaf09fcbb7e4a1f89c37ac`; reconcile any later changes before repinning.

## Required follow-up review

**This patch list is not exhaustive.** Before finalizing the v2.7.0 bump, sweep **all upstream commits after the v2.7.0 tag through the latest upstream HEAD** to identify additional potentially critical fixes. Assess their applicability to OP and add any required cherry-picks to this list; do not limit the sweep to the patches already identified here.

## Required upstream cherry-picks

### Carry forward from the v2.6.0 fork

- [ ] [paradigmxyz/reth#27634](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27634) — **Use trie changesets for all overlays.** Upstream commit [`078d026239a1977f5d79eeb67fa44d2087ebf7e5`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/078d026239a1977f5d79eeb67fa44d2087ebf7e5); currently carried as `68594096cc4b8a53bce48485c56994d59b21642a`.
- [ ] [paradigmxyz/reth#27782](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27782) — **Rewind backward overlay seeks.** Upstream commit [`5868ee478841e1eaffc2fae740b60b7d5a920896`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/5868ee478841e1eaffc2fae740b60b7d5a920896); currently carried as `56c3d375fbbb4543ff1eb702138ad01d672bd0e9`. Apply before #27832.
- [ ] [paradigmxyz/reth#27832](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27832) — **Remove orphaned trie branches.** Upstream commit [`5e309af68bb064eb594807bf8d2b2e6638b91c27`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/5e309af68bb064eb594807bf8d2b2e6638b91c27); currently carried as `5f793856dd20b855973d8cdfa593d774e7534338`.

### Add fixes identified during the v2.6.0 review

- [ ] [paradigmxyz/reth#27530](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27530) — **Time out slow compressed HTTP requests.** Cherry-pick [`d994469b9b88897fe0c6f971d16a59f6bf26001e`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/d994469b9b88897fe0c6f971d16a59f6bf26001e). Prevents incomplete compressed bodies from holding decompression permits indefinitely. Applies when HTTP decompression is explicitly enabled; it is disabled by default.
- [ ] [paradigmxyz/reth#27717](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/27717) — **Never send empty incomplete eth/70 receipts.** Cherry-pick [`42fa3c569ad182914d26db410919d6a10c7b4859`](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/commit/42fa3c569ad182914d26db410919d6a10c7b4859). Fixes receipt responses when a receipt exceeds the soft response limit, including valid large OP deposit receipts. Ordinary OP block sync derives receipts locally.

Both newly identified fixes applied cleanly to the reviewed v2.6.0 fork and passed focused regressions. Recheck application and validation against v2.7.0.

## Preserve fork-specific changes

- [ ] Retain or port the masked-storage-trie regression test: [`d70cc04dab7d337f96080fad1923ec355750c391`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/commit/d70cc04dab7d337f96080fad1923ec355750c391), `test(storage-overlay): cover storage roots over a masked state trie`. This covers the storage-root path used by OP's Isthmus withdrawals root.

Update its v2.6.0 comparison base for the new release and preserve its dependency/security fixes.

## Already included in v2.7.0

These upstream cherry-picks from the v2.6.0 fork are in the v2.7.0 tag and do not need replaying:

topIssues.title: kona-node: missing L2 block during EL catch-up resets the engine in a loop
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

## Summary

When kona-node's execution client is behind its own labels, an L2 block lookup that finds nothing becomes an engine reset. After an EL datadir wipe under a running kona-node, this turns into a loop: every reset walks the sync start back to genesis and re-derives the chain, and finalization stays at genesis. op-node, driving the same EL through the same scenario, resets once and lets the EL sync. **Not yet reproduced deterministically in a unit test.** The evidence is #23440's CI follow-up and two local runs.

## Evidence (#23440, `TestFollowerResyncsFromScratchUnderConsensusClientThatKeptItsHeads/el_sync`)

The follower's op-reth is stopped, its datadir wiped and restarted while its kona-node keeps running. CircleCI job 5705185 failed at the finalized wait after 621 s: `expected head for label=finalized to advance to target=59, but got current=0`.

1. The first consolidation after the wipe finds no block in the empty engine (`Received None block for 186`, `Consolidate(MissingUnsafeL2Block(186))`). That error has `Reset` severity.
2. The reset reads the wiped engine's labels (`unsafe=0 safe=0 finalized=0`). The sync-start search walks back to the finalized block, genesis (`Found suitable L2 safe block l2_safe=0 is_finalized=true is_genesis=true`), so derivation restarts at L1 genesis and rebuilds the chain itself instead of letting the EL sync.
3. Whenever the derived safe head catches up with the EL's canonical tip while the gossip-fed unsafe head is ahead of it, the next consolidation finds `None` again and resets again. Locally this happened 93 and 94 times in four minutes; in CI, every 4 to 8 s.
4. Each reset clears the `L2Finalizer` queue, so finalized stays at genesis until a finalize task lands between two resets (223 s and 282 s locally). In CI the task that landed hit `BlockNotSafe` and the node exited. That crash is fixed separately by #23908.

The issue also noted that the follower's op-reth answered null by number for block 348 while it had received payload 361, and committed blocks in bursts of about six. That makes "unsafe ahead, block below it missing" a normal transient state during EL catch-up, not only after a wipe.

## Mechanism

- [`ConsolidateTask::consolidate`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/edace855db3fdcfced40f6eda2ffe747ee3a39b8/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/consolidate/task.rs#L175-L180) returns `MissingUnsafeL2Block` when the EL has no block at the safe target's height. [Its severity is `Reset`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/edace855db3fdcfced40f6eda2ffe747ee3a39b8/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/consolidate/error.rs#L41).
- The reset's [sync-start search](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/edace855db3fdcfced40f6eda2ffe747ee3a39b8/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/sync/mod.rs#L86-L100) stops at the EL's finalized block. After a wipe that is genesis, so the derivation pipeline restarts from L1 genesis.
- The same path exists in delegated derivation: a delegated safe target below a gossip-advanced unsafe head, while the EL is syncing, resets too. For comparison, op-node's `FollowSource` treats a not-found local block below its unsafe head as "EL sync in progress" and only updates local-safe.

## Expected behavior / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce with kona-engine tasks and mocked Engine API responses: a consolidation target below the unsafe head whose block the EL does not have yet, while the EL is syncing.
- [ ] A block missing below the unsafe head because the EL is still syncing does not reset the engine. Compare with op-node's CL-sync and follow-source handling, and decide whether kona should wait, retarget EL sync, or reset only once.
- [ ] After an EL datadir wipe under a running kona-node, the node lets the EL sync instead of re-deriving from genesis in a loop, and finalization resumes.
- [ ] #23440's datadir-wipe cell passes under kona-node, and its kona skip (which names #23399) is removed or renamed to this issue.
- [ ] Genuine divergence, where a block is missing because the chain reorged, still resets.

## Related

- #23440: the acceptance test and the CI follow-up this issue comes from.
- #23908: fixes the `Finalize(BlockNotSafe)` exit seen in the same run.
- #23912: the delegated-parity verification. Its catch-up runs can hit this loop.
- ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#574: kona treats SYNCING as applied for unsafe payloads. A related way for the unsafe head to run ahead of the EL.

topIssues.title: kona-node: document or resolve the interop local-safe and cross-safe delegated parity gap
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#545.

Under interop, op-node imports local-safe and cross-safe separately (#19330). Kona's delegated derivation copies the delegated safe head into both labels. The tracker requires this parity gap to be resolved or explicitly documented before #545 closes. It does not affect the non-interop test network.

Scope:
- Document the current behavior and its consequences for interop deployments in the kona-node delegated derivation docs.
- Decide whether Kona should import the two labels separately when the delegate exposes them; if so, implement it with a regression test, otherwise record the decision and the conditions under which it must be revisited.

topPRs.title: ci: pilot RWX with shared routing and shadow tests
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
PR validation currently rebuilds op-reth in CircleCI and lacks executed RWX parity evidence. This pilot runs the complete op-reth release producer and its three associated checks alongside shared routing, Go lint/Rust formatting, Go rollup tests and four standard-contract configurations. CircleCI continues to own the required gates.

The op-reth shadow builds both release binaries, runs every selected `reth-optimism-node` test through a nextest archive, generates fresh compact vectors with pinned develop and reads them with the PR binary, and regenerates both superchain snapshots. It uses shared dependency downloads, content caching, separate native tool caches for Cargo targets and sccache, parallel codec compilers, pinned tools and SHA-bound artifacts. Checksum-matching superchain bundles retain their timestamps. Release, integration and codec consumers mount artifacts directly instead of inheriting compiler-cache layers. Every verdict and vector generation executes freshly.

Validation:

- At `0b7935e7339726c1b1166be6372fbf057fb251dd`, [native op-reth CI](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/0d4989f8fc044b48888ba7cdda9e9b2a) passed all four workloads in **6m20s**. All 50 runnable integration cases passed; one explicitly ignored case remained in discovery. Original JUnit identities and outcomes matched [CircleCI job 5625881](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5625881) exactly. All four RWX status checks are green at this head.
- Direct artifact mounts removed both compiler-cache trees from the codec verifier. Its measured preparation fell from 171s at `99ccc76a` to 2s at this head, followed by fresh execution in 5s. The final consumer received a 622 MiB binary artifact and two small vector/provenance artifacts, and its metadata confirmed the PR checkout. Both observations are single samples, with different runner-local layer states.
- Before the bundle/artifact optimizations, the complete RWX run at `d2b90241` took 13m10s initially and [5m58s with warm tool caches](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/2c7e09f8233541869ff6fa8771b3d372). A [forced target-cache probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8545eb684d094e13abc4e91fdab645fe) after bundle retention executed snapshot preparation in 7s, with six Rust sccache hits and zero misses; fresh regeneration still ran for 24s.
- An [empty-target probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8552f40db3314cf282583313806e0be6) produced 263 Rust hits and zero misses in 36s. An [identical-input release rerun](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/be0b0006cd5044c88739ec46cd81f2d6) reused the compiler content cache and finished the release path in 8s, including fresh binary verification. A separate warm release rebuild recorded 27 Rust hits and no misses but still spent 236s compiling/linking; content reuse and incremental reuse have different benefits.
- An [intentional CLI-only test fault](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/add6576e7432497a8a1e3f85a40a8313) failed the task and run, preserved nextest's exit 100, and retained original JUnit and partial coverage. Committed Rust tests were unchanged.
- 22 cache/provenance/report regression tests, 35 routing scenarios, shell checks and RWX configuration validation passed. The final native artifact consumers inherited no op-reth compiler caches; only snapshot regeneration retained Cargo targets.

Implementation coverage is **10/86 expanded PR jobs, about 12%**. The [parity checklist](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-parity-todos.md) and [measurements](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-migration.md#first-hosted-measurements) track representative Rust source-change probes, repeated actual-resource timings and billed usage, smaller tool/compiler layers, and a protected cache-rebuild policy before promotion. Whole-run duration, compiler phases and billed cost remain separate measurements; declared resource classes do not prove identical hardware. Full Go/acceptance producers and consumers, remaining Rust/contracts, routing and identity cutover remain open.

Earlier Go/contract comparisons at `587b4c3a` still need authoritative CircleCI discovery, 178 contract skip reasons and fresh evidence for 17 cached Go cases. Schedules, publishing and privileged writer ownership remain with CircleCI. The cache-only RWX vault has no production credentials and restricted pilot/develop writers; remove the temporary pilot grant and evict pilot cache entries before promotion.

This single draft PR replaces #23141, #23142, #23144 and #23148 and remains the ongoing home for the pilot.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: run live apply and bootstrap on forge by default
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stack 2/7, merge in order: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The whole change, with green CI, is #23647.

The Go script host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has, so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). op-deployer already had an opt-in forge path for live deployments. This PR makes that path dependable and the default for live `apply` and `bootstrap`. Genesis deployments, the L2 genesis, `prepare` and `continue` still run on the Go script host; later PRs of the stack move them.

**Effect on users**

- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` run on forge. `--use-forge=false` still runs them on the Go script host, until #23308 removes the flag. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed: every broadcast sends one transaction at a time.
- As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction.
- forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a live deployment needs the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works, and `--use-forge=false` keeps the Go script host until #23308.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without FFI, with file access only to the artifacts, and forge inherits only the environment variables that it needs (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- The artifacts-locators page no longer lists `tag://` locators, which op-deployer already rejects. The manual Sepolia test script no longer offers the Go script host as its default engine.
- The forge download detects musl, uses `--cache-dir`, and gives a clear error without network access. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time: without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. A compile watcher enforces "never compile" instead.
- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Bundle builds (Docker, melange, `just forge-build`) run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, and fail when a second run would compile: a single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys chains: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass, and forge gives up after a few quick retries.
- The test `RetryProxy` gives a client error (4xx, not 429) to the client at once: forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the retries held each call for about 40 s.
- The `forge` package tests run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Reviews**

go-code-reviewer on the transitional code of this PR and the next two. Fixed: the BREAKING CHANGE text named `tag://` instead of `https://`/`file://` bundles, and `--use-forge=false` had no test (a live subtest now covers it).

**Known limits, not fixed here**

Live deploys could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does (#23306); the #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast`. The RPC URL stays on the command line of forge, which has no environment binding for it. A crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe). A forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23302.

BREAKING CHANGE: `op-deployer apply` and `op-deployer bootstrap` run on forge by default; `--use-forge=false` runs them on the Go script host until a later release removes it. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed. An `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release is refused for live `apply` and `bootstrap`; use `embedded`, or `--use-forge=false` until the Go script host is removed. Go callers replace `ApplyPipelineOpts.UseForge`, `ForgeSlowBroadcast` and `PrivateKey` with `UseScriptHost` (zero value: forge) and `DeployerPrivateKey`; `pipeline.Env`'s `ForgeClient`, `UseForge`, `L1RPCUrl` and `PrivateKey` with `Forge`; and bootstrap's `UseForge` and `ForgeSlowBroadcast` with `UseScriptHost`. `forge.ScriptCaller` returns `(output, error)` without the recompiled flag, and `forge.Client.SlowBroadcast` is removed. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.
